evidence: arXiv 2606.05339 (Owotogbe, Kumara, Iannillo, van den Heuvel, Tamburri, Natella; v1 3 Jun 2026, v2 19 Sep 2026). Sec. 4.3: 'The final dataset comprised 833 confirmed runtime fault threads used for taxonomy construction.' Method is manual taxonomy coding; no reproduction or repair performed.
correction: Location of the 833 quote is Sec. 4.3 (Failure Identification and Filtering), not 4.1-4.5 generally. Nuance: the paper mines fault-fixing threads and uses developers' linked PRs/commits as 'repair evidence'; say it 'does not itself reproduce or repair bugs'.

evidence: Abstract: '66% exhibit code smells, 14.4% contain ten bug patterns overlapping prior research'; study of 1,899 open-source MCP servers. Authors Hasan, Li, Fallahzadeh, Rajbahadur, Adams, Hassan; v1 Jun 2025, v5 Apr 2026.
correction: Full title: 'Model Context Protocol (MCP) at First Glance: Studying the Security and Maintainability of MCP Servers'. Note RESEARCH.md C5 wording ('critical or blocker-level bugs') is not in the abstract; prefer abstract wording 'ten bug patterns'.

evidence: Abstract: 'silent bugs: they lead to wrong behavior but they do not cause system crashes or hangs, nor show an error message to the user.' Tambon, Nikanjam, An, Khomh, Antoniol; arXiv v1 26 Dec 2021, v2 1 Sep 2023.
correction: arXiv page lists no journal ref; published venue (believed Empirical Software Engineering) not re-checked [verify]; cite arXiv year 2021 (v2 2023).

evidence: Page (HotOS 2017, Huang, Guo, Zhou, Lorch, Dang, Chintalapati, Yao) defines gray failure: '...subtle underlying faults, i.e., gray failure rather than fail-stop failure'; key feature 'differential observability'. Nothing about tools/agents.
correction: Cite only for the definition: 'gray failure ... is characterized by differential observability: failure detectors may not notice problems even when applications are afflicted' [Huang 2017]. Present 'silent tool failures are gray failures' as our framing (C3/Owotogbe also uses the term).

evidence: Sec. 2.4: 'execute each collected bug-fix 5 times without internet access. The bug-fixes that yield the exact same test results across all 5 executions are kept.' ('55' is 55 repositories; HTML renders '5 5' from math+text).
correction: Bugs kept only if test results are identical across 5 offline runs; attrition 508 candidates -> 348 -> 341 with environments -> 228 reproducible -> 199 after manual curation (Sec. 2.2-2.5), from 55 repositories. Authors Silva, Saavedra, Monperrus (2024).

evidence: Abstract: 'The BugSwarm toolkit has already gathered 3,091 fail-pass pairs, in Java and Python, all packaged within fully reproducible containers.' Tomassi et al.; ICSE 2019 (arXiv comments).
Abstract: 'only 112/3,091 (3.6%) are suitable to evaluate techniques for automatic fault localization or program repair.' Durieux and Abreu, arXiv 1905.09375 (May 2019).
correction: The 'curation and attrition reporting are needed' part is our inference, not stated in the abstract.

evidence: Abstract's 'Each bug comes with a test suite that can expose the bug.' describes Defects4J, not BugsInPy; BugsInPy: '493 real bugs from 17 real-world Python programs'. arXiv posted 27 Jan 2024.
correction: Attribute the quote to Defects4J as described by BugsInPy; claim: 'BugsInPy, modeled on Defects4J (whose bugs each come with an exposing test suite), offers 493 real bugs from 17 Python programs.' Full title: 'BugsInPy: A Database of Existing Bugs in Python Programs to Enable Controlled Testing and Debugging Studies' (ESEC/FSE 2020 demo [verify]; arXiv 2024).
